clue.text: Listened to the crowd outside after opening

indicators.note: the word for the crowd goes around the other piece, so it sits outside

parts.note: a crowd of animals or people is a herd

indicators.note: the opening of the word after is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone tunes in to the crowd outdoors once things have got going.
explanation.definitionFit: Heard is the past tense of hear, so it means paid attention to sound or took in by ear.

clue.text: Quail left in a mountain church

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed inside the word for the mountain

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A small game bird turns up on the left side of a church high in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quail' looks like the bird, but it is the verb meaning to flinch. BEN is Scottish for a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to shrink back in fear, and to blench is to flinch or recoil the same way.

clue.text: Underworld boss having lock trouble

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A gangland chief has trouble with a door lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a crime lord, but it is Dis, the Roman ruler of the dead; 'lock' is hair, not a door fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is suffering or difficulty, a close synonym for trouble as a noun.

clue.text: An old soldier-there could be a five neater characters

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: the letters of neater could be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: An ex-serviceman muses that five tidier people might exist.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone who served long in the armed forces, typically a former soldier.

clue.text: Keep causing a jam

explanation.surface: Holding on to something leads to a blockage.
explanation.definitionFit: To conserve is to preserve or save; a conserve is also a fruit preserve, a kind of jam.

clue.text: Head of company given a decoration with the queen's insignia

parts.note: MM is the Military Medal, a British gallantry decoration
and means together with
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the queen

explanation.surface: A firm's chief is honoured with a medal bearing the royal monogram.
explanation.walkthrough: MM is the Military Medal and ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A commander is the person in charge, the head of a unit or operation.

clue.text: The person speaking of French miracle working

parts.note: de is the French word for of

indicators.note: the letters of miracle are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes a French miracle in action.
explanation.definitionFit: A declaimer is an orator who delivers speeches in a rhetorical way.

clue.text: He'll give a fellow an alternative

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A man will hand over a colleague or a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is a giver, someone who contributes money, blood or organs.

clue.text: Drink (soft) for a European

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does, with the tongue
P stands for piano, the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: A soft drink is ordered for a traveller from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: '(soft)' looks like it describes the drink, but it is P, piano in music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lapps, or Sami, are a people of northern Scandinavia, so a Lapp is a European.

clue.text: Dark animal cut by trap

indicators.note: the word for the animal is split open by the trap word placed inside it

parts.note: a brute is a beast or animal
a net is a trap for fish or birds

explanation.surface: A dark beast is caught in a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette is a person with dark brown hair, so the word is used for darkness of colouring.

clue.text: Think it's put on?

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a manner is just an act.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to suppose or take for granted, and also to adopt a manner or garment, as in assuming an air.

clue.text: A woman's holding the ring-there's something afoot!

indicators.note: the pronoun holds the ring letter within it

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A lady wearing a ring hints that something is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afoot' usually means happening; here it is literal, on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is literally worn on the foot, so it is something a-foot.

clue.text: Hopeful partisan going to the dogs

indicators.note: something going to the dogs is falling apart, so the letters fall into disorder

explanation.surface: A hopeful supporter is in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopeful' is a noun here: a hopeful is a candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is a candidate seeking a position, just as a hopeful is someone with ambitions.

clue.text: A healer, naturally

parts.note: a healer who works with nature, using plants rather than drugs, and 'naturally' also reads as of course

explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist treats illness with remedies made from plants, so heals by natural means.

clue.text: Set right about clothes

parts.note: re means about or concerning
dress means clothing

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a matter concerning outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to remedy or put it right.

clue.text: For, he could not ope his mouth, but out there flew a trope" (Butler's'Hudibras)

definitions.text: For, he could not ope his mouth, but out there flew a trope" (Butler's'Hudibras)

parts.words: For, he could not ope his mouth, but out there flew a trope" (Butler's'Hudibras)
parts.note: a quotation from Butler's comic poem with one word left out after For; the missing word is the art of elaborate speech

explanation.walkthrough: The full lines of Samuel Butler's Hudibras put the missing word straight after 'For', describing a speaker who cannot open his mouth without a figure of speech coming out.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted lines describe speech packed with tropes, the stock in trade of the art of persuasive oratory.

clue.text: More gullible, but at the same time more colourful

explanation.surface: Someone is more naive and also more vivid.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or naive, so the comparative is more naive; it also means more verdant in hue.

clue.text: Throw it on a car as a protection in bad weather

indicators.note: to throw the letters is to toss them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice to cover a vehicle with a sheet when it is stormy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw it on' reads like putting on a coat, but 'Throw' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat for wet days keeps the wearer dry when it pours.

clue.text: Make bold page start again

parts.note: to resume is to begin again after a pause

explanation.surface: Someone takes the liberty of telling a pageboy to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make bold' is an old idiom for daring to do something.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to dare or take the liberty, which is what making bold means.

clue.text: An opponent's aim-the gold

parts.note: an object is an aim or goal
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A rival is targeting the gold medal.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An objector is someone who raises opposition to a plan.

clue.text: To the heartless it's a gambling device

indicators.note: the word the with its heart removed keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gambling machine is aimed at the callous.
explanation.walkthrough: A tote is the totalisator, the machine pooling bets at a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The totalisator is a betting system run by machine at racetracks, the source of the name.

clue.text: Dream a little beside a river

indicators.note: only a little of the words beside a is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone dozes briefly next to a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream can be an ambition or notion, a thought held in the mind.

clue.text: Blunders out of needless terror so regrettable

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: Mistakes caused by pointless panic are much to be regretted.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors are mistakes, which is what blunders means as a noun.

clue.text: One's to be found in an English or Mediterranean plant

indicators.note: the first piece is found inside the other pieces

parts.note: one is I, and the 's stands for is, giving I then S

explanation.surface: Something is located in an English or southern European garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise is an aromatic herb native to the eastern Mediterranean, grown for its seeds.

clue.text: A boor about 50 calling a strike?

indicators.note: the phrase for a boor goes about the numeral

parts.note: a lout is a boor, giving A then the word
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A loutish man of about fifty is urging workers out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About 50' looks like an age, but it is the container signal around L.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-out strike involves every worker, so union leaders call one.

clue.text: Getting rugs nice with special treatment

indicators.note: giving the letters special treatment rearranges them

explanation.surface: Carpets are made attractive by careful cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Securing means obtaining, as in securing a contract, the same as getting.

clue.text: Moving music absorbs the holy man

indicators.note: the music word takes in the saint's letters

parts.note: an air is a tune, a piece of music
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Emotional music is taken in by a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like touching, but here it means stirring about.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion.

clue.text: The eccentric bares arms-for shame!

indicators.note: an eccentric is off-centre, so the letters are put off their usual order

explanation.surface: An odd man rolls up his sleeves, to everyone's shame.
explanation.definitionFit: To embarrass someone is to make them feel ashamed, which is to shame them.
